Hi Sasha — quick answers to your bullets and some implementation notes.

1) Egress IP ranges:
- Hosted mode: we publish a small set of egress NAT IPs for customer allowlists. Those ranges are provided in our Network IPs doc and we can provide a CIDR list for your firewall.
- Private/VPC endpoints: preferred. We support AWS Interface VPC Endpoints (ENIs) + internal DNS so traffic never leaves your VPC. This avoids NAT/egress constraints.

2) mTLS + cert rotation:
- Redwood supports mTLS for Private deployments. We accept certs signed by customer CAs or we can run a managed rotation where Redwood holds certs in our KMS and rotates on a scheduled cadence.
- If you use HashiVault we can integrate via a small bootstrap step (CSR generation + Vault PKI issuance). We also expose an API for cert rotation events so you can sync rotation in your infra.

3) Internal DNS:
- Yes, you can point a Route 53 private hosted zone to the VPC endpoint DNS names. We provide a vanity hostname (e.g., redwood-api.prod.finlytics.internal) to make mapping simple.

Implementation sketch (high level):
- Option A (recommended): Create AWS Interface Endpoint(s) in Finlytics-prod subnets that will route to Redwood Private regional LBs. Configure Route 53 private zone to alias the vanity hostname to the endpoint. Use mTLS for service auth.
- Option B: Public egress with IP allowlist and NAT gateway; restrict by our published egress ranges and use API key + MTLS for service auth if preferred.

Auth/SDK notes:
- SDK supports API key header (Authorization: Bearer <key>) for hosted users. For Private customers we recommend mutual TLS with short-lived certificates for machine-to-machine calls (gRPC and HTTPS).
- We will provide a sample SDK snippet for mTLS and a Node/Python example for structured output + tool calling.
